account: Today has mostly followed my appointment book: office correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, tea with my neighbour, and a return to the office. Yet there are signs of preparations whose purpose I have not established. My neighbour passed along Townsfolk Two's report of lights going up at the bakery. The neighbour also said the builder described his work as ordinary supplies and lighting for the hall. Now my secretary has actually seen lanterns placed in the hall, although its central table chest was empty. The secretary could not find the builder at his workshop, so there is still no confirmed explanation. I also overheard freight seeking the innkeeper about a supply order; I do not know whether that connects to the lighting. The lack of accounts or council papers at my accounts appointment was odd, though the secretary now says today's office record is in our chest. My neighbour was welcoming at tea but offered no further confirmed news. I suspect preparations for some gathering or celebration, perhaps involving the hall and bakery, but that is only a guess. I have no evidence of the occasion, its organizers beyond the builder's reported involvement, or any deliberate effort to keep it from me. I should read the office record and seek the builder's own explanation rather than treat rumours as facts.
